title: Implement FT-002 lifecycle grant services and persisted permission adapter
verify: Farm display, Plant create/rename/archive/restore, and grant create/reactivate/update/revoke follow the canonical role and lifecycle matrices.
Engineer creation commits Plant, stable active creator grant with approval false, and both required audit records atomically; injected failures roll back all four.
Archive/restore and grant mutations lock and recheck current DB state and ActorContext in the write transaction; stale snapshots cannot authorize a change.
Archive/restore preserves every grant ID/status/approval flag; grant changes while archived remain non-operative until restore.
Persisted snapshot provider feeds the existing FT-001 resolver and fails closed on missing, mismatched, revoked, archived-normal, and repository-error paths.
FT-002-BHV-002 and FT-002-BHV-003 are covered by executable evidence.

evidence_required: role and lifecycle policy test output
Engineer atomic create success and injected rollback evidence
archive row-lock/current-state and grant preservation evidence
persisted ActorContext snapshot and fail-closed evidence
focused access-admin and full pytest output
constraints: Extend the existing FT-001 PlantPermissionContext DTO and resolver contract; do not create a second permission model.
Use same-transaction AdminAuditRecord writes and current-state row locks for every actual mutation.
Do not implement HTTP, FT-003 account/admin behavior, retained-history payloads, downstream workflow tables, or Safety Gate logic.
Do not weaken no-existence-leak denial on repository errors or relationship mismatch.
invariants: Boss permission is role/Farm based; Engineer and Consultant require an active matching grant.
Engineer creator access is immediate but never includes lifecycle/access management or Safety Gate clearance.
Archive changes only Plant status and grants remain stable/non-operative until current restore and authorization.
Failed and no-op commands write no misleading or duplicate success audit.
verification_targets: Prove persisted ActorContext parity for Boss, Engineer, Consultant, active/revoked grants, and active/archived Plants.
Prove every actual service mutation has the exact same-transaction audit count and every failure/no-op has none.
purpose: Implement the single transactional service boundary that makes the FT-002 authority schema usable through the verified FT-001 ActorContext seam.
success_outcome: Authorized Farm/Plant/grant transitions are atomic, audited, race-aware, and immediately reflected by one fail-closed persisted Plant permission adapter.
anti_goals: No parallel permission or audit model.

stop_conditions: TASK-012-T3-FT-002-W1 is not done or its schema differs from the canonical storage spec.
A mutation cannot recheck current authority/state in the same transaction.
The existing FT-001 ActorContext seam must be broken or duplicated to proceed.
Atomic audit/rollback or no-leak behavior cannot be proven.
